svg.title: One claim, traced back to the sentence and the URL it came from
svg.desc: Three panels read left to right. The first is a page as the extractor left it: its URL, its title, a note that the extracted text runs to 134 words, and the body, with one sentence outlined in green rather than filled, because it is still the page's own words. The second panel is CitationLog.add, the only door a claim can pass through to reach a report. Three ticks record what it checks: that the claim is not empty, that the URL is not empty, and that whether the claim appears in the source text is verified rather than assumed. Passing all three returns a Citation. Below it, a branch taken when the URL is blank leads to a red-outlined box: a MissingSourceError is raised and nothing is appended, so an unsourced claim is never recorded and then filtered out later. The third panel is the resulting citation as JSON, carrying the claim, the URL, the title, and a verbatim flag set true. A dashed return path runs from the third panel back to the first, showing that any claim in the finished report can be walked back to the sentence, the page and the URL it came from. Three closing lines note that the report is assembled only from the citation log, that no code path exists by which an unattributed claim reaches the caller, and that a model's paraphrase is still cited but is recorded with verbatim false and is not quotable.
svg.text: Provenance enforced by the type, not promised in a docstring. An unsourced claim cannot exist.
The regulator has opened a twelve-week
outlined: the sentence the summarizer chose
walk any claim back to the sentence, the page, and the URL it came from
The report is assembled only from the citation log, and the log refuses a claim that carries no source.
There is no code path by which an unattributed claim reaches the caller, because there is nothing to filter.
A model's paraphrase is still cited. It is recorded with verbatim false, and it is not quotable.
